title: US appeals court blocks Minnesota law barring 'nudified' photos in XAI lawsuit
source_used: Reuters (wire text read on the syndicated copy at Devdiscourse)
key_facts: On Friday (2 Oct 2026) the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals, based in St. Louis, put Minnesota's ban on AI-generated fake nude images on hold.
It granted a request for an injunction made by Elon Musk's xAI.
Reuters describes the Minnesota law as the first-in-the-nation ban of its kind.
xAI is pursuing a lawsuit that argues the law is unconstitutional; the lawsuit continues.
A lower-court judge had rejected xAI's request for an order stopping the law last month.
Reuters describes xAI as a technology and social media company.
quote_evidence: The St. Louis-based 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals in its order put the law on hold, granting a request for an injunction by Musk's xAI.
A lower court judge last month had rejected Musk's bid for an order stopping the law.
why_it_matters_hint: Minnesota's first-of-its-kind ban on AI-made fake nude images cannot be used for now while the constitutional challenge goes on.
